chunks: And al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar and Sa'd, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah and Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: concerning

Concerning a man who performed tayammum, he said: “That suffices him until he finds water.” And this report remains upon its generality, because he did not restrict it to one time rather than another; rather, he stated unconditionally that it suffices him until the time he finds water.

key_terms.الْخَبَرُ: the report or hadith being cited as legal evidence
key_terms.الْمَاءَ: water, whose availability ends the sufficiency of tayammum
key_terms.تَيَمَّمَ: performed tayammum, the dry ablution used in the absence of water
key_terms.وُجُودِهِ: its being found or becoming available
key_terms.يُجْزِيهِ: is sufficient for him and fulfills the required act

ai.seo_question: Does tayammum remain valid until water is found?
ai.summary: This report states that tayammum is sufficient for a person until water becomes available. Its wording is general and unrestricted, indicating a legal ruling in ritual purity and worship without limiting it to a particular time.
